title: Discovering Piezo1 and Piezo2
objective: Describe how Piezo channels were identified and why Piezo2 is central to touch and gut mechanosensation.

steps.title: A screen for a touch channel
steps.body:
In 2010 the Patapoutian lab found a cell line that made currents when poked, then knocked down candidate genes one by one until the current disappeared. The gene was **Piezo1**; a relative, **[[Piezo2]]**, turned up in sensory neurons.

Both are large channels that open directly to mechanical force, the long-sought mechanotransducers.

steps.title: Piezo2 carries light touch
steps.body: Mice lacking Piezo2 in sensory neurons (2014) lost most of their response to gentle touch. Piezo2 is now considered the **major transducer of innocuous touch** in mammals, part of the work recognized by the 2021 Nobel Prize (A3-L1).

steps.prompt: A cell line makes a poking-activated current. You remove one gene and the current vanishes; add the gene back and it returns. What can you conclude?
options: That gene is necessary and sufficient for the mechanically activated current in these cells
steps.explanation: Loss plus rescue is strong evidence that a gene encodes (or is essential for) the current. This is the logic that identified Piezo channels.

steps.setup: You want to test whether Piezo2 carries gentle touch in the skin.
options: Conditionally delete Piezo2 in sensory neurons and test light-touch responses
steps.reveal: A conditional knockout in sensory neurons isolates Piezo2's role there. That experiment showed light touch collapses without it.

sources.note: Discovery of Piezo1 and Piezo2 mechanically activated channels.
Piezo2 is the major transducer of light touch in mice.
